answer.location_description: Small square patch near the top-left corner of the image, rows 1-3 and columns 1-3.
answer.mechanism: Two groups of layer-1 units read the 3x3 patch. Large-blob detectors (units 1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 18, 20, 24, 27, 28) give it strong positive weights. Small-blob / background detectors (units 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26, 29, 31) give it strong negative weights. In layer 2, u1 collects the first group (e.g. +91 from unit 28, +76 from 27) and has output weight +91. u9 collects the second group (+99 from 26, +88 from 21, +82 from 25) and has output weight -83. So a bright patch both excites the large-blob pathway and suppresses the small-blob pathway, which pushes the logit toward class 1.
answer.evidence: Rows 1-3, columns 1-3 carry weights of about +50 to +93 in units 1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 28 (e.g. unit 18: 83, 86, 92; unit 24: 93). The same pixels carry about -45 to -99 in units 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26, 29 and 31 (e.g. unit 12 r3c2 = -99; unit 29 r1c2 = -96). Inside these units the patch is sharply isolated: the pixels around it are ordinary noise-level weights (or the background sign), with no smooth spatial structure. A blob near the centre cannot reach this corner, so the patch is unrelated to blob size. Its sign in each unit always matches that unit's role: positive in units that also weight the central disk/annulus positively, negative in units that weight the annulus negatively and the background positively.
answer.main_feature: Blob size is read from an annulus around the centre (roughly rows 5-18, columns 5-18). Large-blob units weight this ring positively; small-blob units weight it negatively and give positive weight to the surrounding background. Layer 2 then contrasts these two groups.
